inputs.question: Q.1 (10 marks) A company bought machinery for Rs 1,000,000 on 1 July 2024. Required: compute the depreciation charge for the year ended 30 June 2025 and explain the treatment.
inputs.userAnswer: Straight-line over the machine's useful life of 5 years gives Rs 200,000 for a full year; the asset was held for 12 months of the year to 30 June 2025, so the charge is Rs 200,000. The residual value of nil is used because the source states the machine has no resale value.
inputs.suggestedAnswer: Reducing balance at 20% per annum: Rs 1,000,000 x 20% = Rs 200,000 charge for the year.

inputs.userAnswer: Deductions reduce the tax burden. Allowances given by the employer are deductible and so are expenses incurred in earning the salary. Taxable income is therefore Rs 900,000, which shows the taxpayer has planned well.
inputs.suggestedAnswer: Compulsory (per official scheme): name two deductions (2 marks), quote the exact wording of the section for each (4 marks), compute 1,200,000 - 300,000 = 900,000 (4 marks). The scheme states the quotation of wording is compulsory.

inputs.question: Q.1 (12 marks) A plant carried at Rs 26,000,000 (cost 40,000,000) is revalued on 1 January 2025 to Rs 30,000,000. Required: determine the carrying amount after the revaluation and explain where the movement is reported.
inputs.userAnswer: Cost 40,000,000 less accumulated depreciation 14,000,000 is 26,000,000. The valuation is 30,000,000, so the carrying amount becomes 30,000,000 and the 2,000,000 increase goes to the revaluation surplus, not to profit or loss. The surplus is not taken to profit or loss.
inputs.suggestedAnswer: The asset is restated to 30,000,000; the 2,000,000 increase is recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in equity under revaluation surplus (IAS 16).
